Bisphosphonates may be indicated for patients with Paget’s disease of bone (p.1086) if bone pain is persistent, or to prevent further progression of the disease. Initial experience was with etidronate, but bisphosphonates that have less effect on bone mineralisation may be preferred. In studies, alendronate1 and risedronate2 were found to be more effective than etidronate. 1. Siris E, et al. Comparative study of alendronate versus etidronate for the treatment of Paget’s disease of bone. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 1996; 81: 961–7. 2. Miller PD, et al. A randomized, double-blind comparison of rise- dronate and etidronate in the treatment of Paget’s disease of bone. Am J Med 1999; 106: 513–20. Preparations USP 31: Etidronate Disodium Tablets.
